hypothesis: Without a heat file the CUDA chain's warm start holds the experts in index order, no conversation's, and the promotion brake (no promotion while the last 64 decode steps found 75 % or more of their routes on the card) stops a conversation where the promotions were still paying; starting the brake off without a heat file makes a chat faster on a T4 holding 6605 of 10240 experts, and leaves a run with a heat file as it was.
command: bench.c built against c/ (cd c && make <objects> CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75, as the record's setup); COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./qwen36-bench --model <model> --session chat.sess

hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 cores / 8 threads) + NVIDIA Tesla T4 (15360 MiB, sm_75, up to PCIe Gen3 x16)
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Google Colab, T4 high-RAM), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07

config.session: chat: 5 turns, 1458 answer tokens teacher-forced, through the server's path
config.tok_s: answer tokens / the session's seconds (prompts, first steps and decode, bench's sum)

quality.method: make -C c check (macOS arm64); on the T4 and on the RTX 3070 with the code measured make -C c cuda-test cuda-chain-check, tests/test_qwen36_cuda_chain and tests/test_qwen36_tier_promote pass. The same prompts and teacher-forced answers in every run of both versions; the session's teacher-forced loss is 1.2799 nats a token for both (bench's report). The promoted experts run on the card's kernels instead of the CPU's, so the logits move in the last digits (cli.txt: the same greedy text as dev with the brake at 0)
